locus_audit.detail: G17 explicitly adds ∀e∈E∃p∈P PREDOMINATES(e,p), beyond Q1/Q2. That formula does not require two elements to predominate in different people, does not assert pairwise distinct owners, and does not state strict comparative dominance; the prose gloss 'different elements predominate in different persons' is stronger than its displayed formula. Source lines 176 body14–18 support differences in predominance across persons, but the packet's exact quantified distribution remains an additional, underspecified choice rather than a consequence of the fixed ALL frames.

ARISE_FROM(constitution-name domain, predominant-element-contribution attribute) is a schematic relation. It does not identify a person, name that person's dominant element, or state a pointwise naming/inclination rule; this is consistent with the packet's explicit unresolved note.

The bracketed ALL PERSONS / benefited-by / ALL TREATMENTS / NOT frame matches F2 and olchey's fixed broad scope, giving NOT(forall p forall t BENEFIT(p,t)). This is weaker than universal failure for each person or each treatment. The third group's transcript remains ambiguous under GDT1044, so the fixed formula cannot establish a canonical reading.

The displayed lexicon types qokal as Datum × Criterion → QualifiedDatum, while P0 is a Proposition. An ordinary application of that signature to P0 is a type mismatch. G12 separately declares a proposition-plus-qokal criterion frame, so the candidate can be parsed only by treating G12 as a special signature/coercion for qokal; it is an authored extra construction, not a consequence of the lexicon signature. Even with that extension, 'constitution is relevant to the NOT-ALL proposition' remains a proposed semantic attachment whose source adequacy is expressly unresolved. This is a typed interface problem masked only if G12's special frame is accepted, not evidence that the source entails the tail.

The candidate possibility of voluntary conduct contrary to the constitution domain fits the declared weak modal ceiling and keeps source syntax uncertainty. It does not bind a particular person to that person's constitution or assert successful self-correction; no overclaim found.

W.22a's follow relation is only domain/attribute level. W.22b–23 explicitly quantifies all persons as mixed and inclined, which fits common membership, but the bare INCLINED(p) formula does not encode inclination toward that person's dominant element. The needed person-specific owner bridge is absent from the fixed formulas, as SOURCE_COVERAGE acknowledges.

The postposed ALL PERSONS can span the clause only by G10, an added license correctly called unresolved. In the lexicon, otody is Attribute(Element,Set(Effect)); the displayed O24 formula instead uses PredominantElementContribution(p), a person-indexed datum. No declared constructor maps a person's predominant element to this contribution term, and G10 does not change otody's declared owner type. Thus the formula needs an additional composition/type bridge beyond its prose scope rule. Common membership as a regimen criterion is also an inference rather than an express source instruction, as the packet admits.
